g.text: Each extra Miller-Rabin round makes a wrong "prime" rarer
Measured with this repo's code: for each bar, random.seed(2020), then 50,000 numbers drawn at random from the
16 Carmichael numbers below 10^5 (all composite). Bar height = share of draws the test answered "prime".
log scale: one line down = 10 times rarer
Fermat is wrong three times out of four on these numbers. One Miller-Rabin round is already wrong only about
1 time in 18, and every further round divides that again, well under the guaranteed (1/4)^T.
